# Independent audit: joint critical distal profiles

Audited source:
`candidate 0354c832e0d018af`.
The ordinary distal theorem and the exact symmetric-padding example were
also read in their source files.

**Result: PASS.**

The same Gamma_d applies to both full-dimensional covered bodies. Their
actual halfspace traces cover the bodies according to the sign of the
integer drift, and the same index family retains q_i+U_i+V_i=Q. Adding
ordinary distal bounds at the nonnegative thresholds tau and Q-tau yields
exactly

    |K|+|A| <= Q/Gamma + sum_i[(q_i-tau)_+
                              +(tau-q_i-V_i)_+].

The displayed absolute-value-minus-cross-credit identity is correct for
both q_i>=tau and q_i<tau. It also equals the distance to the closed
interval [q_i,q_i+V_i]. Every interval lies in [0,Q]. Empty, supporting,
proper, and full cap traces retain their actual volumes throughout; no
section derivative is used. The three-cap specialization at the middle
q-value is correct even with ties.

The two-cap overlap/gap signs and exact identity also check: positive sum
of integer slopes gives overlap at the plus endpoint and gap at the minus
endpoint. The ordinary middle traces partition their fiber up to a null
boundary. Thus 2Q=M+overlap-gap and Q>Gamma M/2 in the nonheavy regime
for d>=2. No original cap direction is discarded.

The centroid claims under a hypothetical failure use strict no-heavy
correctly: every pair of fiber volumes exceeds M/2, and M/2-|K| is less
than either endpoint volume. Hence a middle-centroid-containing critical
cap strictly misses both endpoint centroids and has both endpoint masses
below their own centroid guarantees. The coarea density
sup H_(d-1)(section)/||u|| has the correct functional-thickness units; it
is finite and positive for every full-dimensional body and u!=0,
including d=1. Fubini proves the signed gap lower bound with no smoothness
assumption. All drift and positive-minus-negative compensation signs in
(12)--(15) are correct.

The explicit example's convex body, full cap table, centroid margins,
normal balance, strict no-heavy values, and root deficit check exactly.
Its global criticality is supported by the independently proved paired
slice identity in the cited source. It is explicitly distinguished from
a below-OC example.

No correction to the audited source is needed.

## Exact optimization of the joint profile

The following elementary reduction can be appended to that valid profile.
Let I_i=[l_i,u_i] be m closed intervals in [0,Q]. List all their endpoints,
with multiplicities, as e_1<=...<=e_(2m). Then

    min_{0<=tau<=Q} sum_i dist(tau,I_i)
      = (sum_{j=m+1}^{2m}e_j-sum_{j=1}^{m}e_j
                                -sum_i(u_i-l_i))/2.       (1)

Every tau in [e_m,e_(m+1)] is a minimizer. Indeed

    dist(tau,[l,u])=(|tau-l|+|tau-u|-(u-l))/2,

and the sum of 2m absolute deviations is minimized on its median
interval; pairing the j-th smallest with the j-th largest proves both
its minimum and the entire minimizer interval. All endpoints lie in
[0,Q], so the constrained minimization adds no restriction.

For m<=3 there is a simpler exact formula:

    min_tau sum_i dist(tau,I_i)
       = (max_i l_i-min_i u_i)_+.                       (2)

If the intervals intersect this is zero. Otherwise put L=max l_i,
R=min u_i, so L>R. An interval ending at R and one beginning at L are
distinct and force at least L-R distance in total. If a third interval
exists, its lower endpoint is at most L and its upper endpoint at least
R; hence it meets [R,L]. Choose tau in that intersection. The third
interval contributes zero and the two extreme distances sum exactly to
L-R. The argument with no third interval is identical. This proves (2),
including degenerate intervals and repeated endpoint values.

For the actual profile, l_i=q_i and u_i=q_i+V_i=Q-U_i. Thus, for at most
three critical caps covering K and A, the optimized joint inequality is

    Q/Gamma+(q_max+U_max-Q)_+ >= |K|+|A|.                (3)

Under strict no-heavy and Q<Gamma M/2 the right side exceeds Q/Gamma,
so the positive part is strictly active and (3) becomes

    (1/Gamma-1)Q+q_max+U_max >= |K|+|A|.                (4)

This uses maxima from the SAME actual cap family. It does not assert that
the maximizing indices coincide or that either cap also contains another
fiber centroid. For four or more intervals, replacing (1) by (2) would be
false; four point intervals at 0,0,1,1 have minimum distance two but
extreme gap one.
